subject: Political Science (Code: 323)
past_paper_reference: CUET UG Political Science Past Papers (2022-2024)

questions.question: In the first Lok Sabha elections of 1952, which non-party category of contestants secured 37 seats, finishing second only to the Congress in seat tally?
options: A) Independent candidates
B) Communist Party of India
C) Socialist Party
D) Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party
questions.explanation: Independent candidates won 37 seats in the first Lok Sabha in 1952, exceeding the tally of any single recognized opposition party.

questions.question: Which historic memoir detailing the diplomatic merger of princely kingdoms was authored by senior civil servant V.P. Menon?
options: A) 'Discovery of India'
B) 'The Story of the Integration of the Indian States'
C) 'India Wins Freedom'
D) 'The Great Partition'
questions.explanation: V.P. Menon authored 'The Story of the Integration of the Indian States' (1956), providing a firsthand account of Sardar Patel's integration campaign.

questions.question: In 1968, Professor P.C. Mahalanobis was conferred which prestigious civilian honor by the Government of India for his foundational contributions to science and national planning?
options: A) Bharat Ratna
B) Padma Bhushan
C) Padma Vibhushan
D) Padma Shri
questions.explanation: P.C. Mahalanobis received India's second-highest civilian award, the Padma Vibhushan, in 1968 for his services to statistics and economic development.

questions.question: The historic Simla Agreement between Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and President Zulfikar Ali Bhutto was signed in Himachal Pradesh on:
options: A) 16 December 1971
B) 10 January 1966
C) 15 August 1972
D) 2 July 1972
questions.explanation: The Simla Agreement was signed on 2 July 1972 in Shimla, formalizing the outcome of the 1971 war and committing both nations to bilateralism.

questions.topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Who was the President of the Indian National Congress belonging to the Syndicate who expelled Indira Gandhi in November 1969?
options: A) S. Nijalingappa
B) K. Kamaraj
C) Atulya Ghosh
D) N. Sanjiva Reddy
questions.explanation: Siddavanahalli Nijalingappa of Karnataka was the Congress President who led the Syndicate faction during the bitter 1969 split.

questions.question: Morarji Desai was sworn in as the first non-Congress Prime Minister of independent India in which month and year?
options: A) June 1975
B) March 1977
C) January 1980
D) December 1979
questions.explanation: Morarji Desai took the oath of office as Prime Minister on 24 March 1977 heading the newly formed Janata Party government.

questions.question: Before being elevated to a Union Territory in 1972 and a full-fledged State in 1987, the Mizo Hills was administratively an autonomous district within:
options: A) Manipur
B) Tripura
C) Assam
D) Nagaland
questions.explanation: Under the British and in early independent India, the Mizo Hills formed an autonomous tribal district within the state of Assam.

questions.question: In 1987, the Chipko movement was internationally recognized when it was awarded which prestigious international honor often termed the 'Alternative Nobel Prize'?
options: A) Templeton Prize
B) Ramon Magsaysay Award
C) UN Human Rights Prize
D) Right Livelihood Award
questions.explanation: The Chipko movement received the Right Livelihood Award in 1987 for its dedicated dedication to saving India's forests through non-violent collective action.

questions.question: B.P. Mandal, who headed the Second Backward Classes Commission, had earlier served as a Member of Parliament and as the Chief Minister of which state?
options: A) Bihar
B) Uttar Pradesh
C) Madhya Pradesh
D) Rajasthan
questions.explanation: Bindeshwari Prasad Mandal was a veteran socialist leader who briefly served as Chief Minister of Bihar in 1968 before heading the Mandal Commission in 1979.

questions.question: Under the constitutional framework introduced by the 101st Amendment, the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council is chaired by:
options: A) The Prime Minister of India
B) The Union Finance Minister
C) The Governor of the Reserve Bank of India
D) The Chief Minister of the largest state
questions.explanation: Under Article 279A, the GST Council is chaired by the Union Finance Minister and comprises state finance ministers as members, embodying cooperative federalism.

questions.topic: Cold War Era and Non-aligned Movement
questions.question: The Berlin Wall, constructed in August 1961 as the most tangible physical symbol of the Cold War divide, stood intact for how many years before falling in 1989?
options: A) 10 years
B) 15 years
C) 28 years
D) 45 years
questions.explanation: The Berlin Wall divided the city from 13 August 1961 until it was breached on 9 November 1989, standing for 28 years.

questions.question: The circle of twelve gold stars on an azure background, which serves as the flag of the European Union, was originally adopted in 1955 by the:
options: A) League of Nations
B) United Nations General Assembly
C) North Atlantic Treaty Organization
D) Council of Europe
questions.explanation: The flag was designed and adopted in 1955 by the Council of Europe and later embraced by the European Community in 1986 as the official symbol of European unity.

questions.question: In September 1949, the Government of India secured the full merger of Manipur with the Indian Union when Maharaja Bodhachandra Singh signed the Merger Agreement:
options: A) Without consulting the elected Manipur Legislative Assembly, causing enduring local resentment
B) Following a unanimous referendum conducted across all northeastern states
C) After an armed naval invasion of the Imphal river basin
D) Pursuant to a binding judgment issued by the Privy Council in London
questions.explanation: The Government of India pressured Maharaja Bodhachandra Singh to sign the Merger Agreement in Shillong in September 1949 without consulting the elected assembly, fostering separatist grievances.

questions.question: The Congress Socialist Party severed its formal ties with the Indian National Congress to establish the independent Socialist Party at its historic conference held in March 1948 in:
options: A) Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh
B) Nasik, Maharashtra
C) Patna, Bihar
D) Calcutta, West Bengal
questions.explanation: At the Nasik conference in March 1948, socialists led by Jayaprakash Narayan and Acharya Narendra Deva resolved to break away from Congress after Congress amended its constitution to ban dual membership.

questions.question: To supply essential chemical inputs for the High Yielding Variety crops during the Green Revolution, the Union Government established state-owned fertilizer manufacturing plants under the:
options: A) State Trading Corporation
B) National Mineral Development Corporation
C) Fertilizer Corporation of India (FCI)
D) Hindustan Machine Tools
questions.explanation: The Fertilizer Corporation of India (FCI) was formed in 1961 by amalgamating fertilizer units in Sindri and Nangal to provide subsidized chemical fertilizers for intensive farming.

questions.question: In December 1988, Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi undertook a breakthrough official visit to Beijing, agreeing with Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping to:
options: A) Formally cede the Tawang tract in exchange for Chinese recognition of Kashmir
B) Merge Indian and Chinese diplomatic missions in the United Nations
C) Conduct joint military maneuvers along the McMahon Line
D) Establish a Joint Working Group to negotiate the boundary question while developing bilateral trade and cultural ties in parallel
questions.explanation: Rajiv Gandhi's 1988 trip restored momentum to Sino-Indian relations by delinking border resolution from broader bilateral cooperation, creating the Joint Working Group on the border.

questions.topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: In the fourth general elections of 1967, while the Congress retained power at the Centre, its Lok Sabha tally dropped to its lowest level since independence, winning:
options: A) 283 seats out of 520
B) 364 seats
C) 371 seats
D) 154 seats
questions.explanation: The Congress tally dropped sharply from 361 seats in 1962 to 283 seats in 1967, securing only a narrow majority of 23 seats above the half-way mark in the 520-member House.

questions.question: Passed in July 1975 during the Emergency, the 38th Constitutional Amendment Act curtailed judicial power by enacting that:
options: A) The Supreme Court could overrule any parliamentary statute without hearing arguments
B) The President's satisfaction in declaring an Emergency was final, conclusive, and non-justiciable in any court of law
C) All High Court judges were automatically dismissed and placed under police house arrest
D) The Lok Sabha could extend its tenure indefinitely without holding elections
questions.explanation: The 38th Amendment barred courts from reviewing the validity or subjective satisfaction behind proclamations of Emergency or ordinances issued by the President or Governors.

questions.question: Under the terms of the 1985 Rajiv-Longowal Accord, the Eradi Tribunal on river water sharing was instructed to verify the actual usage of waters by Punjab and Haryana as of which date?
options: A) 15 August 1947
B) 26 January 1950
C) 1 July 1985
D) 1 November 1966
questions.explanation: The Accord stipulated that the farmers of Punjab, Haryana, and Rajasthan would continue to receive water not less than what they were using on 1 July 1985 from the Ravi-Beas system.

questions.question: Under sustained domestic and international protest by the Narmada Bachao Andolan, the World Bank in 1991 took the unprecedented step of commissioning an independent review headed by:
options: A) Robert McNamara
B) Paul Wolfowitz
C) Gro Harlem Brundtland
D) Bradford Morse
questions.explanation: The World Bank appointed former UNDP administrator Bradford Morse to head the Independent Review of the Sardar Sarovar Projects, which released a damning report in 1992.

questions.question: The National Front coalition formed in 1988 under V.P. Singh was an umbrella alliance uniting the Janata Dal with prominent regional parties, including:
options: A) Telugu Desam Party (TDP), Asom Gana Parishad (AGP), and DMK
B) Shiv Sena, Shiromani Akali Dal, and AIADMK
C) Muslim League, Kerala Congress, and Revolutionary Socialist Party
D) Bahujan Samaj Party, Samajwadi Party, and Trinamool Congress
questions.explanation: The National Front consisted of the Janata Dal and three regional partners: the TDP (Andhra Pradesh), AGP (Assam), and DMK (Tamil Nadu), with N.T. Rama Rao as President and V.P. Singh as Convener.

questions.question: The Government of India's flagship housing scheme launched in June 2015 to provide pucca houses with basic amenities to eligible urban and rural poor is the:
options: A) Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY)
B) Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY)
C) Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY)
D) Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)
questions.explanation: PMAY was launched in June 2015 with two components: PMAY-Urban (PMAY-U) and PMAY-Gramin (PMAY-G), aiming to provide pucca housing for all eligible families.

questions.topic: Cold War Era and Non-aligned Movement
questions.question: The Cuban Missile Crisis of October 1962 was peacefully resolved through an agreement where the Soviet Union dismantled its missiles in Cuba in exchange for a US commitment to:
options: A) Surrender all US military naval bases in Florida to the United Nations
B) Expel all Western European nations from the North Atlantic Treaty Organization
C) Refrain from invading Cuba and secretly withdraw US Jupiter nuclear missiles from Turkey
D) Transfer control of West Berlin unconditionally to East Germany
questions.explanation: Khrushchev agreed to withdraw Soviet missiles from Cuba after Kennedy pledged publicly not to invade Cuba and secretly promised to dismantle American Jupiter missiles deployed in Turkey.

questions.question: A unique historical feature of the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991, in contrast to earlier imperial disintegrations, was that it occurred:
options: A) Following a decisive nuclear exchange on Russian soil
B) After a total naval blockade imposed by the United Nations Security Council
C) Due to an armed airborne landing by NATO battalions in Moscow
D) Without any direct external foreign military invasion or armed conflict with the capitalist West
questions.explanation: The Soviet superpower disintegrated from within due to internal political, economic, and institutional contradictions and nationalist assertions, rather than external military defeat.

questions.question: During the 1991 Gulf War, precision-guided munitions ('smart bombs') received global media attention because, although they comprised less than 10% of total coalition bombs dropped, they:
options: A) Inflicted disproportionate destruction on key strategic command centers, bridges, and radar sites with pinpoint accuracy
B) Were detonated with sub-critical nuclear yields
C) Were manufactured exclusively by private commercial banks in Switzerland
D) Destroyed all orbital communications satellites in outer space
questions.explanation: While unguided 'iron bombs' made up the bulk of munitions, television footage of laser-guided bombs entering ventilation shafts created the public image of a surgical, high-tech war.

questions.question: The ASEAN Socio-Cultural Community (ASCC), one of the three pillars of the ASEAN Community, focuses primarily on:
options: A) The creation of a common standing naval battle fleet
B) Human development, social protection, environmental sustainability, and regional cultural identity
C) The establishment of a single supranational currency pegged to the US dollar
D) The unification of all Southeast Asian legal penal codes
questions.explanation: The ASCC pillar aims to forge an inclusive, people-oriented ASEAN community by investing in education, poverty alleviation, healthcare, environmental protection, and cultural identity.

questions.question: In 1980, China established its first four experimental Special Economic Zones (SEZs) along its southern coast in Guangdong and Fujian provinces at Shenzhen, Zhuhai, Shantou, and:
options: A) Shanghai
B) Guangzhou
C) Xiamen
D) Tianjin
questions.explanation: The four original SEZs designated in August 1980 were Shenzhen, Zhuhai, and Shantou in Guangdong province, and Xiamen in Fujian province, situated across the straits from Taiwan.

questions.question: The Treaty of Peace and Friendship signed between India and Nepal in July 1950 is distinctive because it grants citizens of both countries:
options: A) Compulsory dual citizenship with joint voting rights in each other's national parliaments
B) The right to serve in a unified nuclear weapons joint command
C) Exemption from all criminal law jurisdictions in both states
D) Reciprocal national treatment regarding residence, property ownership, business, and employment across an open international border
questions.explanation: Articles 6 and 7 of the 1950 treaty grant citizens of each country reciprocal national treatment in matters of residence, business, and property, facilitating an open border between India and Nepal.

questions.question: The United Nations Charter was signed on 26 June 1945 at the conclusion of the United Nations Conference on International Organization in San Francisco by representatives of how many countries?
options: A) 50 participating nations (with Poland signing later as the 51st original member)
B) 12 nations
C) 100 nations
D) 193 nations
questions.explanation: Fifty nations signed the Charter on 26 June 1945 in San Francisco; Poland, which was unable to send a delegation due to government formation, signed on 15 October 1945 as the 51st founding member.

questions.question: In traditional realist security discourse, the core core values that a state must protect at all costs are:
options: A) The market exchange value of private commercial stocks
B) Sovereignty, territorial integrity, and political independence
C) The universal adoption of a single foreign language
D) The tourism revenue of international hotel chains
questions.explanation: Traditional security centers on the survival of the state, identifying threats to state sovereignty, national territory, and political independence as paramount.

questions.question: The computer simulation model 'World3' that provided the empirical basis for the Club of Rome's 1972 report 'The Limits to Growth' was developed by researchers at:
options: A) Oxford University
B) Sorbonne University
C) Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT)
D) Tokyo University
questions.explanation: Dennis Meadows and a team of researchers at MIT used system dynamics models created by Jay Forrester to simulate the interactions of population, industrial growth, food, and resources.

questions.question: Sociological analysis of globalisation reveals that while cultural homogenisation threatens local cultural diversity through Westernisation, globalisation simultaneously produces:
options: A) The total legal abolition of all native mother-tongues
B) The disappearance of all sovereign national flags worldwide
C) The compulsory shutdown of all regional religious places of worship
D) Cultural heterogenisation, where each culture becomes more distinct and hybrid through global cultural exchanges
questions.explanation: Global cultural encounters are not purely homogenizing; they also stimulate cultural self-awareness and hybridity (heterogenisation), as seen in global cuisine, fusion music, and local traditions.

questions.question: In the 1952 general elections, the Communist Party of India (CPI) won 16 seats in the Lok Sabha, performing with notable electoral strength in which regions?
options: A) Madras, Travancore-Cochin, West Bengal, and Hyderabad (Telangana)
B) Punjab, Haryana, and Rajasthan
C) Gujarat and Maharashtra exclusively
D) Jammu & Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh
questions.explanation: The CPI won 16 seats concentrated in areas of agrarian radicalism and peasant movements, such as the Telangana region of Hyderabad, Malabar/Travancore-Cochin, and parts of Bengal.

questions.question: The Planning Commission of India was established in March 1950 as which type of institutional body?
options: A) A permanent constitutional body created under Article 280
B) An extra-constitutional and non-statutory advisory body created by Cabinet resolution
C) A statutory corporation established by an Act of Parliament
D) A judicial tribunal operating under the Supreme Court of India
questions.explanation: The Planning Commission was neither mentioned in the Constitution (extra-constitutional) nor created by a statute of Parliament (non-statutory), deriving its authority from an executive Cabinet resolution.

questions.question: A cornerstone principle of the 1972 Simla Agreement was the commitment by India and Pakistan to resolve all disputes exclusively through:
options: A) Compulsory arbitration by the International Court of Justice
B) Binding resolutions passed by the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation
C) Direct bilateral negotiations without third-party international mediation
D) Direct executive orders issued by the British Commonwealth Secretariat
questions.explanation: Article 1(ii) of the Simla Agreement explicitly establishes that the two countries are resolved to settle their differences by peaceful means through bilateral negotiations, excluding third-party intervention.

questions.question: The police action against the Nizam of Hyderabad code-named 'Operation Polo' commenced on 13 September 1948 under the military command of:
options: A) General K.M. Cariappa
B) General K.S. Thimayya
C) Lieutenant General Jagjit Singh Aurora
D) Major General J.N. Chaudhuri
questions.explanation: Major General Joyanto Nath Chaudhuri commanded the Indian 1st Armoured Division during Operation Polo, accepting the surrender of the Nizam's forces on 17 September 1948.

questions.question: In his landmark 1964 article 'The Congress System in India', political scientist Rajni Kothari described the party system as a 'System of Consensus' because:
options: A) The ruling Congress accommodated competing social factions within itself, while opposition parties acted as peripheral pressure groups that influenced policy through factions inside Congress.
B) All opposition political parties were legally required to vote in favor of every government bill.
C) Parliamentary elections were contested on a single consensual national candidate list.
D) State governors were chosen through unanimous national referendums.
questions.explanation: Kothari demonstrated that the Congress was an open umbrella organization where policy debate took place through internal factions, with external opposition parties acting as pressure groups on those factions.

questions.question: During the drafting of the Second Five Year Plan, which prominent liberal economist on the Panel of Economists submitted a famous 'Note of Dissent' warning against heavy deficit financing and artificial state suppression of consumer goods?
options: A) Professor V.K.R.V. Rao
B) Professor B.R. Shenoy
C) Professor D.R. Gadgil
D) Professor Amartya Sen
questions.explanation: B.R. Shenoy dissented from the Mahalanobis plan framework, arguing that massive deficit financing to build capital goods would cause price inflation, deplete foreign exchange reserves, and misallocate capital.

questions.question: In the aftermath of the military defeat in the 1962 Sino-Indian War and Defense Minister V.K. Krishna Menon's resignation, the Nehru government faced its very first No-Confidence Motion in August 1963, moved by:
options: A) Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia
B) Atal Bihari Vajpayee
C) Acharya J.B. Kripalani
D) A.K. Gopalan
questions.explanation: Independent socialist MP Acharya J.B. Kripalani moved the first-ever motion of no-confidence against the Jawaharlal Nehru government in the Lok Sabha in August 1963 over defense preparedness.

questions.topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: During the 1969 presidential election, the ideological polarization of Indian politics was revealed when official Congress candidate Sanjiva Reddy was supported by:
options: A) The CPI and CPI(M) exclusively against the entire Congress party
B) The Muslim League and Akali Dal exclusively against all national parties
C) The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam and Shiv Sena in joint alliance
D) The Congress Syndicate, Swatantra Party, and Bharatiya Jana Sangh, while V.V. Giri drew votes from Congress (R), CPI, and regional parties
questions.explanation: The Syndicate formed an informal tacit understanding with right-wing parties (Swatantra and Jana Sangh) to back Reddy, prompting Indira Gandhi's radical faction and left-wing parties to rally behind V.V. Giri.

questions.sub_topic: Shah Commission on Delhi Power Cut
questions.question: The Shah Commission's investigation into the imposition of Emergency revealed that on the night of 25 June 1975, electricity supplies to major newspaper offices along Bahadur Shah Zafar Marg in Delhi were disconnected on:
options: A) Oral instructions from the Prime Minister's Secretariat to the Lt. Governor and Delhi electricity authorities to prevent morning editions from reporting opposition arrests
B) A legitimate technical transformer breakdown caused by a severe thunderstorm
C) An executive order signed by the Chief Justice of India under Article 142
D) A strike initiated by the All India Newspaper Employees Federation
questions.explanation: The Shah Commission proved that power was deliberately cut on illegal verbal orders from the PM's office to prevent newspapers from printing news of the arrests of JP, Morarji Desai, and others.

questions.question: Clause 5 of the Assam Accord (1985) classified foreigners in Assam into three distinct streams based on entry dates. How were those who entered between 1 January 1966 and 24 March 1971 to be treated?
options: A) They were to be immediately deported across the international border within forty-eight hours.
B) They were to be detected, their names deleted from electoral rolls for a period of ten years, but allowed to remain in Assam, after which voting rights would be restored.
C) They were granted unconditional permanent dual citizenship with Bangladesh.
D) They were exempt from all local land tax and state criminal procedures.
questions.explanation: Under the 1985 accord, 1966-1971 entrants were detected and disenfranchised for 10 years (retaining other civic rights), while those who entered after 24 March 1971 were to be detected and expelled.

questions.question: Following the critical findings of the 1992 Morse Commission regarding flawed environmental impact assessments and deficient resettlement policies, what decisive action occurred regarding the Sardar Sarovar project?
options: A) The Supreme Court of India ordered the permanent demolition of the dam foundation.
B) The United Nations Security Council dispatched peacekeepers to supervise the dam reservoir.
C) The Government of India asked the World Bank to cancel the remaining loan disbursements in 1993, deciding to complete the project with domestic resources.
D) The Government of Gujarat abandoned all irrigation canal construction permanently.
questions.explanation: Facing harsh international scrutiny from the Morse Report and conditionality deadlines, the Government of India requested the World Bank to cancel the remaining $170 million loan in March 1993.

questions.question: In the Mandal Commission's eleven-point scoring methodology for backwardness, how many total points were available across all categories, and what score designated a caste as socially and educationally backward?
options: A) Total of 100 points available; castes scoring 90 points or more were classified as backward
B) Total of 10 points available; castes scoring 2 points or more were classified as backward
C) Total of 50 points available; castes scoring 45 points or more were classified as backward
D) Total of 22 points available; castes scoring 11 points (50%) or more were classified as backward
questions.explanation: The Mandal Commission established a 22-point scale (Social = 12 points, Educational = 6 points, Economic = 4 points); any caste scoring 11 points or above was determined to be socially and educationally backward.

questions.topic: Cold War Era and Non-aligned Movement
questions.question: The term 'Third World' (Tiers Monde), which came to designate the non-aligned developing nations during the Cold War, was first coined in 1952 by:
options: A) Alfred Sauvy, a French demographer, in an analogy with the 'Third Estate' of the French Revolution
B) Jawaharlal Nehru, in his speech at the Asian Relations Conference
C) Frantz Fanon, in 'The Wretched of the Earth'
D) George Kennan, in his 'Long Telegram' on Soviet conduct
questions.explanation: Alfred Sauvy coined the term 'Tiers Monde' in an article in L'Observateur in August 1952, drawing a parallel to the Third Estate: 'ignored, exploited, and despised, wanting to be something'.

questions.question: The First Chechen War (1994-1996) was brought to a temporary halt through the signing of the Khasavyurt Accord in August 1996 between:
options: A) Boris Yeltsin and Bill Clinton, placing Chechnya under NATO military administration
B) Russian Security Council Secretary Aleksandr Lebed and Chechen military chief Aslan Maskhadov, postponing the decision on Chechnya's official status until 2001
C) Mikhail Gorbachev and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
D) Vladimir Putin and the President of Kazakhstan
questions.explanation: The Khasavyurt Accord ended the first war, withdrawing Russian troops and deferring the formal political status of Chechnya until 2001, though the peace collapsed into the Second Chechen War in 1999.

questions.sub_topic: Susan Strange on US Structural Power
questions.question: British political economist Susan Strange identified four structural pillars of global power. In her framework, US hegemony remains dominant across all four structures, which are:
options: A) Control over Agriculture, Religion, Architecture, and Language
B) Control over Mining, Forestry, Marine Fishing, and Rail Transport
C) Control over Security, Production, Credit/Finance, and Knowledge/Information
D) Control over Monarchies, Feudal Estates, Municipalities, and Guilds
questions.explanation: Susan Strange's structural power model emphasizes that whoever controls security, global production chains, the financial credit system (dollar/IMF), and knowledge/technology exercises enduring hegemony.

questions.question: Under the Qualified Majority Voting (QMV) 'double majority' rule established by the Treaty of Lisbon, a legislative proposal in the Council of the European Union requires the approval of:
options: A) A unanimous 100% vote of all member states without a single abstention
B) A simple majority of 50% of states representing 50% of the land area
C) The approval of Germany and France exclusively, with other votes disregarded
D) At least 55% of member states (minimum 15 states) representing at least 65% of the total EU population
questions.explanation: The Lisbon double majority rule requires 55% of member states (15 out of 27) comprising at least 65% of the EU population, balancing the rights of small states and populous nations.

questions.question: Established in December 2005 following the 2005 World Summit, the United Nations Peacebuilding Commission (PBC) is an intergovernmental advisory body created to:
options: A) Assist nations emerging from violent conflict by mobilizing resources and coordinating post-conflict reconstruction to prevent relapse into war.
B) Deploy autonomous combat drone strikes against non-member rogue states.
C) Directly manage the sovereign central banks of all developing nations.
D) Abolish the veto power of the permanent five members of the Security Council.
questions.explanation: The Peacebuilding Commission fills the gap between military peacekeeping and long-term recovery, providing integrated strategic advice and financial coordination for post-conflict state building.

questions.question: The Scientific Committee on Antarctic Research (SCAR), established under the Antarctic Treaty System, plays which vital governance role?
options: A) It conducts commercial exploratory oil drilling operations in the Ross Sea.
B) It issues commercial sovereign titles for real estate development in Antarctica.
C) It operates naval surface warships to enforce sovereign territorial claims.
D) It coordinates independent, international scientific investigations and provides objective scientific advice to Antarctic Treaty Consultative Meetings on environmental protection.
questions.explanation: SCAR is an interdisciplinary body of the International Science Council that initiates, develops, and coordinates scientific research in Antarctica and advises Antarctic Treaty parties on ecosystem conservation.
